intro: Antwerp rewards visitors with a stunning station, a lively old town, and a strong fashion and art scene. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: De Lijn runs trams, buses, and pre-metro trams; a 10-fare card costs about €21.
Single fares last one hour; pay contactless on board, cash is not accepted.
Ride apps like Uber and Bolt work in Antwerp; taxis wait at the station and main squares.
The centre is compact and walkable; many streets are narrow and slow for cars.
Bikes are popular; cycle superhighways F1, F4, and F14 reach the city.
The city centre is a low-emission zone; register foreign cars before entering.

central_station.name: Antwerp Central Station
central_station.hours: Station hall roughly 05:00–01:00 · check on the day
central_station.tip: Walk up to the middle level and look back down the escalators for the best view of the marble hall.

cathedral.name: Cathedral of Our Lady
cathedral.price_text: About €12 adults · under 18 often free · check on the day
cathedral.hours: Roughly Mon–Fri 10:00–17:00 · Sat 10:00–15:00 · Sun 13:00–17:00 · check on the day
cathedral.tip: Climb the tower only if you are fit; the stairs are steep and narrow.

grote_markt.name: Grote Markt
grote_markt.tip: Sit on the steps by the Brabo fountain and look up at the guild houses at golden hour.

mas.name: Museum aan de Stroom (MAS)
mas.price_text: About €12 for exhibitions · rooftop free · check on the day
mas.hours: Tue–Fri 10:00–17:00 · Sat–Sun 10:00–18:00 · closed Mon · check on the day
mas.tip: The free rooftop walkway gives the best harbour view in the city.

duvel.name: Duvel Moortgat Brewery
duvel.price_text: About €15–25 for a guided tour · booking required · check on the day
duvel.hours: Tours by reservation only · check on the day
duvel.tip: It is outside Antwerp in Puurs; book ahead and check train plus shuttle options.

plopsa.name: Plopsa Station Antwerp
plopsa.price_text: About €15–25 per person · check on the day
plopsa.hours: Roughly daily 10:00–18:00 · check on the day
plopsa.tip: Indoor family park inside the station building; good for a rainy half-day with kids.

tomorrowland.name: Tomorrowland
tomorrowland.price_text: Ticket prices vary by year · check on the day
tomorrowland.hours: Festival weekends in summer only · check on the day
tomorrowland.tip: It is in Boom, not central Antwerp; plan transport and accommodation months ahead.

meir.name: Meir shopping street
meir.tip: Walk from the station to the Old Town and stop at the Stadsfeestzaal arcade.

het_steen.name: Het Steen castle
het_steen.price_text: Free to view outside · visitor centre free
het_steen.hours: Outside always open · visitor centre roughly 10:00–18:00 · check on the day
het_steen.tip: Short riverside stop near the Old Town; good photo of the Scheldt.

scheldt_walk.name: Scheldt river walk and Sint-Anna beach
scheldt_walk.price_text: Free · ferry to left bank small fee
scheldt_walk.hours: Always open · ferry roughly daytime · check on the day
scheldt_walk.tip: Take the ferry across for a skyline view back at the city.

zurenborg.name: Zurenborg neighbourhood walk
zurenborg.tip: Look for the Art Nouveau houses around Cogels-Osylei; quiet residential streets.

theaterplein_market.name: Theaterplein food market
theaterplein_market.price_text: Free to browse · food paid per item
theaterplein_market.hours: Market mornings · check on the day
theaterplein_market.tip: Come hungry and try local cheese and street snacks.

plantin_moretus.name: Plantin-Moretus Museum
plantin_moretus.hours: Tue–Sun roughly 10:00–17:00 · closed Mon · check on the day
plantin_moretus.tip: A UNESCO printing house; quiet and worth an hour for book lovers.

rubenshuis.name: Rubenshuis
rubenshuis.hours: Tue–Sun roughly 10:00–17:00 · closed Mon · check on the day
rubenshuis.tip: Check opening status before you go; the house may be under works.

muhka.name: M HKA contemporary art museum
muhka.hours: Tue–Sun roughly 11:00–18:00 · closed Mon · check on the day
muhka.tip: Modern art in Het Zuid; pair it with a walk along the docks.

het_zuid_food.name: Het Zuid food and bar streets
het_zuid_food.price_text: Free to walk · meals paid per venue
het_zuid_food.tip: Good area for an evening meal and Belgian beer away from the busiest tourist streets.

eilandje_walk.name: Eilandje docklands walk
eilandje_walk.tip: Walk the old docks between MAS and the red-light district edge; watch for cyclists.

beer_tour.name: Belgian beer tasting in the Old Town
beer_tour.price_text: About €25–40 per tasting · check on the day
beer_tour.tip: Ask for local Antwerp brews and small pours; eat first.

vlaeykensgang.name: Vlaeykensgang alley
vlaeykensgang.tip: A hidden medieval alley near the cathedral; keep quiet and do not enter private doors.

sint_paulus.name: Sint-Pauluskerk
sint_paulus.hours: Roughly daytime · check on the day
sint_paulus.tip: Quiet church with a famous Calvary garden; a calm break from the Grote Markt.

station_district_food.name: Station District quick eats
station_district_food.price_text: Free to browse · meals paid per venue
station_district_food.tip: Handy for a fast meal before or after your train; the station area is busy at rush hour.

kmska.name: KMSKA fine arts museum
kmska.hours: Tue–Sun roughly 10:00–17:00 · closed Mon · check on the day
kmska.tip: Big Old Masters collection in Het Zuid; allow at least two hours.

city_guide_walk.name: Old Town guided walking tour
city_guide_walk.price_text: About €10–20 · tip-based tours also exist · check on the day
city_guide_walk.tip: Book a small-group tour early in your trip to get your bearings.

stays.why: Walk to the cathedral, Grote Markt and museums. Best for first-timers.
Quiet streets with galleries, bars and the Museum of Fine Arts nearby.
Next to the grand Antwerp Central station; easy train links and good value.
Old docks, the MAS museum and modern waterfront hotels.

food: Try Flemish classics: stoofvlees (beer-braised beef), vol-au-vent and waterzooi.
Belgian beer is the local drink. Ask for a small tasting glass and try a few.
Waffles and chocolate shops are everywhere in the centre; prices rise near the cathedral.
Look for lunch deals (dagschotel) at cafés away from the Grote Markt for better value.
Book dinner on weekends; popular places in Het Zuid fill up.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a short train ride to Mechelen or Ghent; check times on the day.
Add a half-day at the Plantin-Moretus Museum, a UNESCO-listed printing house.
Take a walk or bike ride along the Scheldt river and the old docks in Eilandje.
